MINUTES
  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE
  NOVEMBER 20, 2024

1.  CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. in the City Hall
  Council Chamber.

2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Brown Schachter, Combs,  Halvorsen,
  Martin, Munday, Nash, Rowe

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Olson, Persichina

  ALSO PRESENT (VIA ZOOM):  Deputy Duran, LACSD

  STAFF PRESENT:  David Wahba, Public Works Director
  Reggie Greene, Traffic Engineering Deputy
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES, FEBRUARY
  22, 2024.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROWE made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER NASH to,

  APPROVE THE TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  FEBRUARY 22, 2024.

There being no objection, CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

NONE

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  PROJECT UPDATES:

  1. PVDN AND DAPPLEGRAY SCHOOL INTERSECTION IMPROVEMENTS

Director Wahba provided an update on the PVDN and Dappelgray School Intersection
Improvements project. There were several workshops to discuss this project, and the project was
approved by the City Council on August 13, 2024. The improvement includes widening the
intersection and adding an additional through lane in each direction, new bus stops with ADA
compliant bus shelters, and new traffic signals; the bridle trail will remain. Director Wahba stated
that this was the last signalized intersection on PVDN that needs improvements. There was a
$2.9M Measure M fund granted for this project. Since the grant was approved years ago,
construction costs have increased; staff have submitted a Metro grant application in the amount
of $1.6M to fund this project. The project is anticipated to begin in the summer of 2026.

COMMITTEE MEMBER HALVORSEN inquired about what would happen if the additional Metro
grant were not approved. Director Wahba stated that there are other funding sources, but this is
the most promising; the South Bay City Council of Governments is focused on projects that are
ready to build, so it is likely that the grant will be approved.

COMMITTTEE MEMBER ROWE asked if there is a possibility for the project to be divided into
two separate contracts in order to begin the project earlier. Director Wahba stated that the issue
in doing this is if the funding for the second contract is not approved, this could result in a half-
built project. He further explained that dividing the project could be more costly.

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  1
Minutes, November 20, 2024
 CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER asked if the school will be contacted to be sure it will not conflict
with their summer school schedule. Director Wahba stated that staff will contact the school to
make sure of this.

  2. ROLLING HILLS ROAD BIKE LANE PROJECT

Director Wahba stated that this project was brought to the Traffic and Safety Committee about
three years ago. The roadway widens enough to accommodate a bike lane on both sides of the
road that are about 5 FT. wide. The City was able to get a $250K grant from Metro for the design
work; the amount spent for the design and environmental work was $300K. The portion of the
roadway extends from the Torrance city limit to PVDN. This project will also extend the pedestrian
walkway and improve the crosswalks at PVDN and mid-block near St. Lukes Church. Director
Wahba stated that the City received a $250K grant for Highway Safety Improvement Programs
(HSIP) and this is for pedestrian improvements along the roadway; it incorporates improving the
push button and flashers. The project has been fully engineered by Willdan. This has gone
through the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) and an Initial Study and Mitigated
Negative Declaration (IS/MND) has been prepared for this project. Notifications were sent to the
Indian Tribes and have requested to be present when any excavation begins. The next steps are
to finalize the engineered plans, release the IS/MND for public comment after the new year, and
present the project to the City Council for approval.

COMMITTEE MEMBER NASH asked about the possibility of this project being extended to other
areas of the city. Director Wahba stated that initially, staff has looked into doing this on Palos
Verdes Drive East. After the Rolling Hills Road project is completed and as funding becomes
available, the project will be extended to Palos Verdes Drive East. The idea is to have bike lanes,
rolled curb and gutters, and improved pedestrian access on all major arterials throughout the City.

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER stated that the Equestrian Committee expressed concern with
visibility and with the speed that vehicles are travelling on Rolling Hills Road and suggested
installing a speed radar. Director Wahba stated that this could be incorporated into the design; he
added that the appearance of a narrow road typically causes vehicles to slow down.

  3. DEEP VALLEY DRIVE CROSSWALK AND REPAVING PROJECT

Director Wahba stated that there has been a delay with the Deep Valley Drive Crosswalk and
Repaving Project due to the completion of the Anastasi condominium project at 927 Deep Valley
Drive. The condominium project has not been completed; however, staff will no longer wait and
the crosswalk and repaving project will move forward. The project includes pedestrian crosswalk
improvements at five locations and street repair and repaving on Deep Valley Drive. The City has
received a Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP) grant of $250K to help fund this project.
The project will go out to bid in January 2025 and construction is anticipated to begin in mid-April
and completed in the summer of 2025. Director Wahba stated that he will be working with Anastasi
on the portion in front of the 927 Deep Valley Drive project since they are responsible for the curb
and gutter, sidewalk work, and bulb out on their side of the street.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY inquired about the placement of the crosswalk since there
were issues with jaywalking from the 627 Deep Valley Drive building to the parking structure.
Director Wahba stated that this considered; however, there are already crosswalks near the traffic
circle, and it is not ideal to have crosswalks placed close together.

Dan Houk, VP La Collina Homeowners Association, stated that there was an accident in front of
627 Deep Valley Drive involving a student crossing the street struck by a vehicle. He expressed
his concern with the location of the proposed crosswalk and stated that most pedestrian traffic on
the street comes from the coffee shop and tutoring center at 627 Deep Valley Drive. Due to limited
parking, pedestrians need to walk across the street to the parking structure and through three
traffic locations.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene stated that he can look into this and will need to see where
the utilities are on the street in order to relocate the crosswalk.

COMMITTEE MUNDAY agreed and added that vehicles line up on both sides of the street.

Director Wahba stated that staff will look into this again and stated that the tutoring center’s
location is an issue due to there being no pick-up or drop-off areas for students.

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  2
Minutes, November 20, 2024
 A brief discussion ensued.

COMMITTEE MEMBER COMBS asked if there is a suggested location for the crosswalk. Mr.
Houk stated that the ideal location would be directly in front of the Kumon Tutoring Center (at 627
Deep Valley Drive). Director Wahba added that this way, pedestrians do not need to cross any
driveways.

Mr. Houk stated that another issue is that vehicles are always double-parked in front of the
building making it difficult for vehicles exiting the 627 Deep Valley Drive building to see cross
traffic. Director Wahba stated that this has been discussed and the Sheriff’s have been patrolling
the area; however, vehicles still park in the red/in front the fire hydrant.

Lynn Yen, Resident, if the city has/could speak to the school about having volunteer escorts for
the kids. Director Wahba stated that staff can suggest this to the school.

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER stated that a letter from the City expressing concern would be a
good idea. Director Wahba stated that he would draft a letter to Kumon.

  NEW ITEMS FOR DISCUSSION:

  1. PVDN TRAFFIC AND SIGNAL TIMING STUDY RESULTS

Director Wahba stated that the PVDN at Dapplegray School Intersection Improvement Project
should alleviate some congestion on PVDN. Since COVID ended and school started up again,
the traffic on PVDN has become unbearable. Staff was asked to look at signal timing to improve
traffic flow.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene provided the results of the signal timing study. The study was
done using video surveillance for seven days at the intersections of PVDN and Crenshaw Blvd.,
Rolling Hills Road and PVDN, and PVDN at Dapplegray School (London Lane). Additionally, there
were bi-directional volume counts and speed data collected at various locations. The preliminary
finding is that there are no issues with the signal timing; the issue is the volume of vehicles and
not enough lanes. Mr. Greene stated that it was observed that vehicles would back-up and clear
in a few signal cycles; he will be taking a look at why this is happening. It was also observed that
more vehicles travel west bound than east bound throughout the day.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene stated that a request was received to look at historical data,
and there is an engineering traffic survey from 2021. CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER stated that
this would be helpful to explain if an increased volume of traffic is the issue.

Director Wahba stated that some may think that the issue is making the vehicles at Rolling Hills
Road turning onto PVDN should wait longer; this has already been looked into and the vehicles
on Rolling Hills Road already wait quite a while for the signal to turn.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER COMBS, Director Wahba stated that the
signals do not communicate with each other at this time, but this is something that staff is looking
into. Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene explained that there are several ways to have the traffic
signals synchronized; the most modern approach is to have the signals communicate with each
other. Director Wahba explained that currently the signals work on loops and detect traffic
changes and the signals timing changes accordingly.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY asked about the timing for the signal at Dapplegray School
and the possibility of having a flashing yellow instead of a red light for those exiting the school.
Director Wahba stated that this is not part of the project but can be looked into at a future time.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene stated that the next step in finalizing the PVDN traffic and
signal timing study is to verify the data, research and compare the historical with current data,
and provide a report including any recommendations.

  2. REQUEST FOR ADDITIONAL “NO RIGHT TURN ON RED SIGNS” AT PVDN AND
  PVDE

Director Wahba provided background and stated that currently the southwest corner of PVDN
and PVDE sign is “No Right Turn on Red” seven days a week from 7a.m. – 6p.m. There have

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  3
Minutes, November 20, 2024
 been no recent complaints about the sign, and it seems people are getting accustomed to the
restriction.

Director Wahba stated that there has been a request for a sign at the northwest corner of PVDN
and PVDE and explained that the geometry is different at this corner. A solution may be to add a
Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI) at this intersection which will allow a few seconds for
pedestrians to enter the intersection prior to a motorist making a right turn. This would be for all
four corners.

COMMITTEE MEMBER COMBS stated that he favors the “No Turn on Red Sign” due to known
near accidents at this intersection.

Ms. Yen explained that this is a tricky right turn to make, but she has seen a near accident at this
intersection as well.

COMMITTEE MEMBER HALVORSEN asked if there could be a green arrow at this intersection.
Director Wahba stated that this would require adding another signal and changing out the
equipment.

COMMITTEE MEMBER HALVORSEN inquired about lighting at the intersection. Director Wahba
stated that he will look into this since it has come up in the past.

Ms. Yen commented that there may be more activity when Founders Park opens and suggested
that both the “No Turn on Red” sign and the LPI may be an option. Director Wahba inquired if the
volume of pedestrians will merit looking into a crossing guard. Ms. Len stated that it depends on
the time of day.

A brief discussion ensued.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene stated that you will begin seeing LPI’s at more intersections
since it has become State law, not yet for local agencies; City of Los Angeles has begun to
implement it.

COMMITTEE MEMBER COMBS made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER ROWE
to,

  RECOMMEND THE FOUR SIGNALS AT PVDN/PVDE TO BE REPROGRAMMED WITH
  LEADING PEDESTRIAN INTERVAL.

AYES: Brown Schachter, Combs, Halvorsen, Martin, Munday, Nash, Rowe
NOES:
ABSENT: Olson, Persichina
ABSTAIN:

Director Wahba stated that this will be presented to the City Council for consideration at its
December 10 meeting.

6.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

NONE

7.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

COMMITTEE MEMBER HALVORSEN asked for information on the recent storm drain project on
PVDE. Director Wahba stated that this was an American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funded project.
A number of storm drain lines were replaced from Club View Lane on both sides of the street to
Bridlewood Circle. The intent is to take the storm water from north of PVDN to the City Limit to
treat it through three infiltration basins before it is discharged to Machado Lake. This will reduce
pollutants going into Machado Lake and will open the Bridle Trail; there should not be any more
issues when it rains. Signs will be installed for authorized City Vehicles access only and a three-
rail fence will be installed.

Director Wahba stated that there has been a delay in finalizing Founder’s Park due to a change
of contractor. The Grand Opening for Founder’s Park is scheduled for December 10, 2024.

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  4
Minutes, November 20, 2024
 CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER stated that Rancho Palos Verdes (RPV) has implemented first
and second warnings, and third violation a fine of $150 for e-bikes and asked if this should be
discussed at the next Traffic and Safety Committee meeting. Director Wahba stated that Jessica
Slawson, Assistant to the City Manager, is working on this to take to City Council for consideration.
CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER suggested having Ms. Slawson attend the next Traffic and Safety
Committee meeting to provide status.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROWE stated that he attended the RPV meeting and there was concern
that the ordinance applies to anyone age 14 and older but anyone under 14 can still ride an e-
bike on the sidewalk. It was voted on and approved the way it was written. COMMITTEE
MEMBER ROWE stated that this is something to consider when it is being considered for RHE.

There was consensus among the committee to invite Assistant to the City Manager Slawson
attend the next Traffic and Safety Committee meeting to provide information on e-bike restrictions.

8.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER adjourned the meeting at 7:46 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,  Approved by,
